## Two ways to calculate the scalar product {#iv5-geometric-rule .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson}

Choose the formula that matches **what you know**.

<div class="g-method-grid">
<div><h3>Know the components?</h3><p>For <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}=(a_x,a_y)"></span> and <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{b}=(b_x,b_y)"></span>:</p><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=a_xb_x+a_yb_y"></span></div><p>Multiply matching components, then add.</p></div>
<div class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><h3>Know the lengths and angle?</h3><p>Use the tail-to-tail angle <span data-math="\theta"></span>:</p><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta"></span></div><p>Multiply the two lengths and the cosine of the angle.</p></div>
</div>

<div class="fragment g-method-conclusion" data-fragment-index="1">
<div class="g-rule g-equivalence"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=a_xb_x+a_yb_y=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta"></span></div>
<p class="g-method-message">Both calculate the <strong>same scalar (dot) product</strong>.</p>
</div>
<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 5.1 · Geometric expression for the scalar product · p. 37</div>

::: notes
Keep this comparison entirely in 2D. Initially show only the components method. One click on Next (or the right-arrow key) reveals the lengths-and-angle method; a second click reveals the complete equality and the conclusion. A third click moves to the 3D slide. Previous reverses these steps. The component expression is a_x b_x+a_y b_y, including b_x in the first product. Components are useful when coordinates are supplied; the geometric formula is useful when lengths and their included angle are supplied. The equivalence follows from Example 5.1. Angle statements assume both vectors are non-zero. If either is zero, the component scalar product is zero.
:::
